object_description: elongated three-part volume with pent roofs on a lowered base
design_condition: The building sits orthogonally to the neighborhood at the southern perimeter, stays close to the western neighbor, preserves distance to the north, and uses a slightly lowered base to create two access levels.

positive.statement: The placement generates a pleasantly large distance from the northern parcel while retaining good topographical connections.
The volumetrically differentiated appearance is consistent with the school's function.
All units have ground-level access, with clearly separated entrances and functional organization.
The stair connections between the two uses are plausibly solved.
The two-story base levels are illuminated on both sides and can be used throughout.
The floor plan offers exciting spatial experiences and enables work on separate levels.
The supporting structure largely follows an economical principle.
The expected construction costs are in the lower range of the shortlisted projects.

negative.statement: The base theme with an overlying body is not rigorously worked out, and the independent roof structures are hardly implemented.
The wooden facade seems strange in the neighborhood.
The sunken, narrow outdoor space is not attractive.
The day school is concentrated on a limited and unsatisfactory outdoor space.
The stair connections are probably too steep.
The acoustic separation of the main room from the gallery is questionable.
The roof terrace is difficult to see from the main room.
People with walking difficulties have the longest route to the entrance level, and the elevator is far away.
The connection between the southern and northern garden rooms is insufficient.
The potential of the sunniest outdoor area is not exploited and its design is left undefined.
The mixed construction volume implies higher gray energy, while the energy and building-technology concept is unclear.
Some day-school rooms receive insufficient daylight and the sun protection is inadequate.
The permissible building depth is exceeded in the basement.
